name: nosana-mcp

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Checks the API key, credits, and every Nosana API this server uses. Call it first when something fails; it returns the exact fix. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Credits on the Nosana account behind the API key: assigned, reserved by running deployments, settled (spent) and available. 1 credit is priced like 1 USD. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Ready-to-run Nosana templates (MiniMax H3 video, Qwen and Gemma LLMs via Ollama, DeepSeek via vLLM, ComfyUI, Jupyter, VS Code, Whisper, ...) with kind, VRAM needs and variants. Templates with variants need a variant id when deploying. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

search.description: Filter by id, name or category, e.g. "minimax", "qwen" or "LLM".

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Details of one template or variant: kind, VRAM needed, hardware notes (e.g. MiniMax H3 needs a Blackwell GPU), exposed ports, typical boot time, variants, and optionally the job definition and README. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

template.description: Template id or name, e.g. "minimax-h3" or "minimax-h3/i2v-32gb".

tools.name: list_gpus
tools.description: GPU markets bucketed the way a buyer shops: ready_now (fits and idle host available), fits_but_queued (fits, nobody idle), idle_with_risk (idle but a caveat), unsupported (cannot run this workload). Prices per hour include the network fee and match deploy.nosana.com. Pass a template so the buckets reflect its VRAM and hardware needs. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

template.description: Template id, optionally "id/variant", to bucket by its requirements.

min_vram_gb.description: Bucket by a VRAM requirement instead of a template.

include_queue.description: Also read on-chain queues to report jobs waiting per market (slower).

verbose.description: Also return the full flat list and too-small GPUs.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: One call from a workload name to a ready-to-confirm plan. Accepts "minimax-h3", "minimax-h3/i2v-32gb", "qwen3-6-27b", "gemma3 27b", "comfyui/sdxl" or a job_definition. Returns the resolved template, GPUs in buckets, the cheapest GPU that is ready now with its cost, any similar deployment already running, and the exact create_deployment arguments. Never picks a queued or unsupported GPU on its own. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

workload.description: Template id/name, optionally with "/variant", or a loose description like "qwen 27b".

tools.name: estimate_deployment
tools.description: Dry run of create_deployment with the same arguments: resolves workload and GPU (including gpu="auto"), validates, and returns the cost for one timeout window plus blocking warnings. Nothing is created. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

template.description: Template id or name, e.g. "minimax-h3" or "minimax-h3/i2v-32gb" (see list_templates or recommend_plan). Omit when passing job_definition.

variant.description: Variant id, e.g. "i2v-32gb". Required when the template has variants.

job_definition.description: A custom Nosana job definition object instead of a template.

gpu.description: GPU market slug, short name or address ("nvidia-5090", "5090"), or "auto" for the cheapest GPU that fits and has an idle host right now.

timeout_minutes.description: Minutes the GPU is reserved per job. Minimum 60. Default: 120 for workloads that download weights, else 60.

strategy.description: SIMPLE runs once and stops at the timeout (predictable cost). SIMPLE-EXTEND keeps extending while credits last. SCHEDULED needs schedule. INFINITE keeps a replacement job ready.

schedule.description: Cron expression (5 fields). SCHEDULED strategy only.

include_community_gpus.description: Allow community GPU markets, not only the premium ones the dashboard shows.

tools.name: create_deployment
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS. Creates a Nosana deployment from a template or job definition on the chosen GPU (or gpu="auto" = cheapest fitting GPU with an idle host) and starts it. Requires confirm=true, which you must only pass after the user has seen the estimate and agreed. Refuses when no host is idle unless accept_queue=true, when a similar deployment is already running unless allow_duplicate=true, and on hardware or credit problems unless force=true. Then poll wait_for_deployment. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

template.description: Template id or name, e.g. "minimax-h3" or "minimax-h3/i2v-32gb" (see list_templates or recommend_plan). Omit when passing job_definition.

variant.description: Variant id, e.g. "i2v-32gb". Required when the template has variants.

job_definition.description: A custom Nosana job definition object instead of a template.

gpu.description: GPU market slug, short name or address ("nvidia-5090", "5090"), or "auto" for the cheapest GPU that fits and has an idle host right now.

timeout_minutes.description: Minutes the GPU is reserved per job. Minimum 60. Default: 120 for workloads that download weights, else 60.

strategy.description: SIMPLE runs once and stops at the timeout (predictable cost). SIMPLE-EXTEND keeps extending while credits last. SCHEDULED needs schedule. INFINITE keeps a replacement job ready.

schedule.description: Cron expression (5 fields). SCHEDULED strategy only.

include_community_gpus.description: Allow community GPU markets, not only the premium ones the dashboard shows.

confidential.description: Hide the job on the explorer and protect the endpoint with an auth header.

start.description: Start immediately. false leaves a DRAFT (drafts cannot be deleted until started once).

confirm.description: Must be true. Confirms the user approved the estimated cost.

accept_queue.description: The user agrees to wait for a host when the GPU has none idle.

allow_duplicate.description: Create even though a similar deployment is already running.

force.description: Deploy despite blocking warnings (too little VRAM, unsupported GPU, insufficient credits). Unsupported hardware will most likely fail and still bill the boot time.

tools.name: wait_for_deployment
tools.description: Watches a deployment for up to max_seconds (default 30, max 45; MCP clients time out at 60 s). Returns outcome "online" (service answers, with ready URLs and usage), "completed" (job finished, with logs), "stopped" (stopped by the user or its timeout; not an error), "failed" (with the scheduler error) or "pending" (with phase, elapsed time and poll_after_seconds; call again). Safe to call repeatedly. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: get_deployment
tools.description: Current status and phase of a deployment: endpoints (tunnel online and whether the service actually answers), ready URLs, price per hour, recent jobs and events, and what to call next. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: get_endpoint_usage
tools.description: Explains how to use a running deployment: ComfyUI UI and /prompt API, OpenAI-compatible base URL for Ollama/vLLM LLMs (OPENAI_BASE_URL, /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions), Jupyter/VS Code URLs, or the raw ports of a custom job. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.description: Deployments on this account (newest first) with status, strategy, active jobs and timeout. Check status=RUNNING before creating another one. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: stop_deployment
tools.description: Stops a deployment and its running jobs. Billing stops with them. Use when the user is done or when a deployment can never schedule. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: start_deployment
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS. Starts a DRAFT or STOPPED deployment again with its existing settings (pays the boot time again). Requires confirm=true after the user agreed. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: extend_deployment
tools.description: Sets a new timeout in minutes for a deployment (minimum 60). Longer timeouts reserve more credits. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

tools.name: get_job_result
tools.description: Logs and results of a deployment job (latest job by default). Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

job.description: Job address; defaults to the latest job.

tools.name: get_deployment_events
tools.description: Scheduler event log for a deployment (job listed, stopped, errors such as insufficient funds or bad timeout). Newest first. Returns JSON: {ok, message, next_tool, next_args, ...tool-specific fields}.

instructions: Nosana MCP rents GPUs on the Nosana network and deploys ready-to-run templates (MiniMax H3 video, Qwen/Gemma/GPT-OSS LLMs, DeepSeek, ComfyUI, Jupyter, VS Code) or custom job definitions, paid with the account credits behind the API key. 1 credit is priced like 1 USD. Start with recommend_plan(workload). Prefer GPUs in ready_now (fits, idle host). Queue on a fits_but_queued GPU only if the user accepts waiting (accept_queue=true). Use an idle_with_risk GPU only if the user accepts the caveat (force=true). Never use an unsupported GPU. Always show the user the estimated credits and USD per hour before create_deployment, and pass confirm=true only after they agree. Check running_similar first; do not stack a second copy of the same workload without asking. Nosana refuses timeouts under 60 minutes. Poll wait_for_deployment with max_seconds <= 45 and relay the phase to the user; big templates take 5 to 15 minutes to download weights. outcome "stopped" means the user or the timeout stopped it, not a failure. Every response is a JSON object with ok, message, and next_tool/next_args suggesting the next call. When the workload is online, call get_endpoint_usage and hand the user the URL plus how to use it. Idle deployments burn credits: remind the user to stop_deployment when done.
